Firms receive a high quality score only when net liquidity is sufficient to offset the magnitude of their overhead adjustment mismatch.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cumulative Capital-Maintenance Capacity
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose cumulative after-depreciation operating income and current liquidity jointly cover cumulative capital consumption earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Combining multi-period earnings with the current liquidity reserve eliminates the highly correlated oiadp/at and oiadp/dp bottleneck legs. The cumulative denominator measures sustained capital consumption, reducing sensitivity to one unusually small depreciation observation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Residual-Liquidity Organizational Capacity
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), ADD(dp, xint)), xsga), 3), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: High operating margins are more valuable when liquidity remaining after reserving for depreciation and interest can still support organizational expenditure.
considered.reasoning: This imposes an explicit funding sequence: net liquidity first absorbs capital-consumption and financing commitments, and only the residual supports SG&A. It therefore tests discretionary organizational capacity after fixed charges rather than directly recombining archived SG&A, fixed-charge, and runway ranks.

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially cash-based operating profitability (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev 2016) crossed with the Sloan accrual anomaly, and the binary INDICATOR collapses every gate-failing firm to exactly zero, so the bottom of the cross-section conflates "high-profit but accrual-heavy" with "unprofitable," destroying the ranking's economic ordering.

The MIN bottleneck of a five-period downside profitability floor and low leverage is internally consistent and the sign is right, though both legs are individually well-mined (profitability and leverage/distress) so the incremental content rests entirely on the TS_MIN "durability" twist rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

The two legs are near-mechanical duplicates — the change in retained earnings *is* net income less dividends, so TREND(re/at) is largely a smoothed restatement of the profitability leg it multiplies, making this a redundant self-interaction rather than a cross-theme conditioning signal.

A coherent DuPont-flavored composite (margin conditioned on turnover stability) with a correctly signed, non-degenerate construction, but the fundamental-volatility leg overlaps heavily with documented earnings-stability/low-risk effects, so novelty is moderate rather than high.

This is not a cross-theme interaction at all but a single rescaled profitability ratio — oiadp/lt is mechanically ROA times an inverse-leverage factor — making it a trivial denominator swap on the standard profitability anomaly with added small-denominator instability for near-debt-free firms.

The expression, hypothesis, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent and the multiplicative form genuinely targets a joint fragility state, but the resulting construct is a close proxy for the published financial-distress anomaly, so it should be judged on whether it beats a simple leverage or earnings-volatility baseline.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's best signal ("Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength") with MA(·,3) mechanically swapped for TS_MIN(·,3) — the same two legs, same MIN combiner, and the "floor" idea already appeared in "Solvent Profit Floor" — so it tests an estimator window rather than a new economic mechanism.

The near-term-claims leg (xint + dlc) is a genuinely different conditioning variable from the archive's total-leverage and debt-change legs, though it awkwardly adds a flow to a stock and the overall profit-meets-low-debt template remains close to "Solvent Profit Floor," so upside over the existing result is likely modest.

re/at is largely cumulative past profitability (and a well-worn lifecycle/Altman-style distress proxy), so the two MIN legs are highly correlated by construction and the weak-link adds little beyond a repackaged profitability sort with a known distress screen.

COALESCE(xrd,0) assigns the large non-reporting majority the bottom R&D rank, so the MIN mechanically restricts the high end to R&D reporters and the signal degenerates into the known R&D-intensity anomaly conditioned on profitability, while the stated "sustaining research without cutting it" hypothesis (a change/persistence idea) is not what the level of xrd/sale computes.

oibdp/at and pi/at are near-collinear so the "survives to pretax income" screen is largely vacuous, leaving a profitability × low-total-liabilities sort that duplicates "Solvent Profit Floor" with a slightly broader leverage denominator.

Δ(act−lct)/at is essentially the working-capital accrual, so NEG of it is the low-accrual leg that Sloan's anomaly says predicts *higher* returns — combined with rising ΔROA (also positively predictive in the earnings-change literature), the expression's high end should earn positive, not negative, abnormal returns, contradicting the stated EXPECTED_SIGN.

Economically coherent and distinct from the archive's low-burden screens, though the second leg is dominated by cash-flow-to-assets and therefore risks partially rediscovering cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016), and mixing a flow (oancf) with a stock (dlc) makes the "coverage" interpretation loose.

This is a cosmetic variant of the already-evaluated Solvent Profit Floor — the same profitability∧low-leverage bottleneck with oiadp/sale swapped for oibdp/at and dltt/at swapped for (dltt+dlc)/at — so it is unlikely to teach anything new.

Since revt−cogs−xsga is definitionally oibdp (oiadp plus depreciation), this is essentially Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength with a pre-depreciation numerator, i.e. a near-rediscovery of an existing archive signal rather than a repair of the failed overhead-stability design.

A defensible level-vs-change reframing of the accrual-light signal, but note that MA(DELTA(WC/at),3) telescopes to a scaled three-year working-capital change and the level-profitability∧low-accrual combination sits close to the well-known profitability and accrual anomalies, so incremental content is limited.

Because ceq/lt is a monotone transform of liabilities-to-assets, IND_RANK makes the second leg rank-equivalent to NEG(lt/at), so this reduces to the same profitability∧low-leverage bottleneck already tested as Solvent Profit Floor rather than a genuinely new "capital adequacy" dimension.

Internally consistent (high signal = simultaneous profit deterioration and rising current claims, hence the negative expected sign) and a substantive departure from the failed volatility×leverage design, though a MIN-of-two-bad-signals construction leaves the short leg economically heterogeneous and both legs are single-period changes with attendant noise.

This is essentially the archived "Current-Debt-Covered Profit" with dlc swapped for dltt and a three-year cash-flow sum, i.e., the same profitability × cash-coverage-of-debt bottleneck rather than a substantively new mechanism, and the flow-minus-stock leg is dominated by the well-known low-leverage and operating-cash-flow-to-assets effects.

Very close to the archived "Liquid-Claim-Covered EBITDA Margin" (margin × liquid-claim coverage) with a difference-form buffer instead of a ratio, and it double-counts leverage because pretax margin already subtracts interest expense while the second leg re-penalizes funded debt.

The coverage leg is copied verbatim from an archived signal and the profit-count leg is the classic Piotroski/quality "years profitable" screen, which as a 0–5 integer produces massive rank ties and lumpy, unstable portfolio composition.

Pairing a profitability trend with a deleveraging trend is a defensible and internally consistent departure from the archive's level-profitability × debt-change signals, though the debt-trend leg substantially overlaps the published net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and three-point TREND estimates will be noisy.

The sign flip on SG&A is properly motivated by the archive's contrary evidence and "profitable despite heavy SG&A" is a coherent organization-capital screen, but it leans on a known intangible-investment anomaly and the triple-MIN structure repeats a construction that previously delivered near-zero alpha and thin coverage.

The ABS in the denominator breaks the stated economics—deeply loss-making firms with large negative OIBDP receive a low "fragility" score and are excluded from the short leg—so the expression contradicts the hypothesis, and what remains is largely capital intensity plus leverage, i.e., a repackaged distress/asset-heaviness effect.

Since dlc is a subset of lct, MA((act−dlc)/at) is nearly collinear with the archived "Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength" leg MA((act−lct)/at), making this a cosmetic component swap rather than a new mechanism test.

This is the already-evaluated "Liquid-Claim-Covered EBITDA Margin" with its first leg mechanically volatility-adjusted using the operator from another archive entry, so it is very likely near-collinear with prior results and offers no genuinely new economic question.

A defensible test of whether intangible-style SG&A intensity pays off specifically when working-capital efficiency is improving, though it is largely the intersection of two archived signals and the triple MIN will thin coverage and mechanically fight the shared-sale-denominator tension between margin and SG&A intensity.

Replacing the liability-intensity trend with its recent worst level is a coherent, diagnosis-motivated shift from change to persistent level, but the resulting leg is close to the low-leverage screens already tested (e.g., Solvent Profit Floor), limiting expected incremental information.

oiadp/MAX(oibdp,dp) equals 1−dp/oibdp for profitable firms, so it ranks capital/depreciation intensity rather than profitability as the hypothesis claims, and it is essentially the sign-mirrored version of the already-tested and weak "Capital-Consumption Liquidity Stress."

Trending current-debt concentration is a distinct maturity-structure channel not already in the archive (which tested only its level), though a 3-point annual TREND is noisy and the profitability leg is a standard ROA screen.

This is a single-leg substitution (MA → MA−VOL) inside the archive's best-performing "Liquid Organizational-Investment Profit" triple, i.e. a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal with high correlation to it, and it inherits the unresolved contradiction that the archive treats high xsga/sale as both a positive (organizational investment) and a negative (overhead burden) attribute.

A genuinely new pairing of two independently supported legs (capital productivity oiadp/dp and improving maturity structure) that were never combined, though it remains a leg-recombination within a saturated MIN-bottleneck template and the oiadp/dp ratio is unstable for small-dp firms even after winsorization.

Replacing MA with TS_MIN on the margin leg of the archive's "Worst-Case Claim-Efficient Margin" is a near-mechanical variant (3-period mean and minimum of a slow-moving margin are highly collinear) and is unlikely to diagnose the earlier fmb/alpha divergence.

This just adds a level screen on dlc/lct to the already-tested "Maturity-Extended Operating Profit," and level and trend of the same ratio are mechanically opposed at the extremes (firms with already-minimal current-debt share have little room to decline), so the extra leg mostly shrinks coverage rather than adding an independent mechanism.

The expected sign is in tension with both the accruals literature and this archive itself — rising current liabilities *lowers* working-capital accruals (which the archive's "Accrual-Light"/"Low-Accrual" signals treat as good), and the closely related "Short-Term-Pressure Profit Erosion" already produced a slope opposite to the hypothesized direction.

Swapping act/lct for act/(lct+dltt) in the already-evaluated "Capital-Productive Liquid Earnings" is a robustness check on a nearly identical coverage ratio rather than a new economic interaction, and the proposal's own reasoning concedes as much.

This is essentially the archive's "Liquid Organizational Productivity" (oiadp/xsga × net-working-capital) with dp merged into the denominator — a cosmetic denominator tweak of an already-tested 3.5-t signal rather than a new mechanism, and the pooled xsga+dp scaling muddles rather than resolves the SG&A sign ambiguity it claims to address.

This is the most substantively distinct proposal in the batch — it shifts the debt-covered-cash channel from levels/trends to a two-leg one-lag change concordance with a coherent diagnosis of the prior signal's sparse coverage — though the unsmoothed annual DELTAs will be noisy and the second leg conflates cash-flow improvement with current-debt reduction.

Pure leg-swap: both components (oiadp/xsga productivity and NEG TREND(dlc/lct)) already appear in tested archive signals, and the same pairing with oiadp/dp ("Capital-Productive Maturity Improvement") returned a weak ls_talpha of 1.70, so this is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new hypothesis.

Mechanical recombination of two already-evaluated legs ("Worst-Case Claim-Efficient Margin" and the oiadp/dp productivity family); the stated motivation of pairing a strong-alpha leg with a strong-FMB leg is a generic combinatorial argument, not an economic reason the interaction should be sharper.

The second leg is verbatim the archive's "Debt-Service-Resilient EBITDA" constraint and the first is the same xsga+dp variant proposed above, making this a redundant within-batch and within-archive leg swap on a profitability × near-term-debt theme already tested at least four ways.

Direct leg-swap of "Low-Accrual Profit State" (identical accrual leg, oiadp/at replaced by the already-tested oiadp/dp), and the underlying profitability-plus-low-accruals combination is close to a rediscovery of the well-known Sloan accrual and quality-score anomalies.

This is a single-operator edit (dropping ABS) of the archived Flexible-Cost Liquid Margin with both other legs identical, so despite a defensible cost-stickiness rationale it is a cosmetic variant whose information content will largely overlap the parent, and the un-absolute leg also collapses toward a known SG&A-growth-versus-sales-growth efficiency screen.

Recycling two archived legs is incremental, but the COGS-versus-revenue co-movement term is genuinely new content (effectively gross-margin stability rather than overhead flexibility) and the construction is internally consistent with the stated positive sign.

The middle leg's natural direction is wrong — high depreciation intensity is a capital-intensity/investment proxy generally associated with *lower* expected returns, so demanding it be high for a positive-sign signal contradicts the investment-anomaly evidence, and the required intersection of high dp/at with high act/lct will produce a small, unstable, industry-conflicted long leg.

The two legs are mechanically opposed (high-margin firms have small COGS, hence mechanically high lct/cogs), so the MIN largely selects on a denominator artifact, and what survives is a generic margin-plus-low-current-liability screen already spanned by archived Low-Refinancing-Risk Margin and Overhead-Liquidity Fragility.

This is a pure leg swap that replaces the liquidity term of archived Flexible-Cost Liquid Margin with the debt-maturity trend term of archived Maturity-Extended Operating Profit, i.e. a recombination of two already-tested components with no new economic content.

This is effectively the archived Liquid-Claim-Covered EBITDA Margin with a small interest deduction in the numerator and dltt dropped from the coverage denominator — interest expense is an order of magnitude smaller than OIBDP for most firms, so the margin leg is near-identical and the expected incremental evidence is minimal.

This is essentially the archive's "Debt-Issuance-Adjusted Fixed-Charge Profit" with the scaler switched from assets to the (dp+xint) denominator borrowed from "Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage," a recombination of two already-tested constructs rather than a new mechanism, and the Δdebt subtraction mechanically rewards deleveraging firms (a known net-debt-issuance effect) rather than isolating coverage.

Since oibdp−dp ≈ oiadp, this is the already-evaluated "Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength" (MA(oiadp/at,3) bottlenecked by MA((act−lct)/at,3)) with only interest expense subtracted—a cosmetic variant of a signal that already delivered fmb 2.98 / alpha 3.6%.

Identical in structure to the archive's "Liquid Organizational Productivity" (oiadp/xsga × net-liquidity bottleneck) with only xint netted out of a numerator that is otherwise oiadp, so it is a marginal tweak rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The construction is internally coherent and the sign direction is natural, but it differs from the archive's "Liability-Neutral Operating-Cost Cash Return" only by swapping the denominator from (cogs+xsga) to (dp+xint)—a scaler substitution with additional small-denominator instability—rather than testing a new economic channel, and it inherits that signal's already-thin ~6-7% coverage.

Both legs are lifted verbatim from prior evaluations (the stability-adjusted profitability leg from "Continuous Profit Reliability" and the debt-issuance-adjusted coverage leg from the first proposal in this batch), so while the pairing is new and economically sensible, it is a derivative leg-swap whose incremental information over the tested versions is likely small.

The two MIN legs share the identical numerator (oibdp−dp−xint) and differ only in scaler, so they are highly collinear and the "interaction" mainly reduces to sorting on after-charge earnings twice; the stated protection against small-denominator dominance is not achieved because the lct leg still mechanically favors firms with tiny current liabilities.

Mechanically near-equivalent to the archived "Funded Organizational Runway" — since oiadp/xsga × xsga/sale = oiadp/sale, jointly requiring high ranks on the first two legs simply selects very-high-margin firms, leaving the identical xsga/sale and (act−lct)/xsga legs to do the work.

The runway denominator is dominated in magnitude by xsga for most firms, so this collapses to a two-leg version of the archived "Funded Organizational Runway"/"Fixed-Charge Liquidity Runway" pair rather than adding a distinct economic commitment.

This is essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive signals ("Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage" and "Fixed-Charge Liquidity Runway"), and its two coverage legs share the identical dp+xint denominator, so the added leg contributes little independent information.
This is the archived "Flexible-Cost Liquid Margin" with its financial-health leg swapped for another archived liquidity leg — precisely the cosmetic leg-substitution the reasoning claims to avoid.

The cleanest and most internally consistent of the batch, with dp as a shared capital-maintenance yardstick for both earnings and liquidity, but it is still the same MIN(profitability, coverage, coverage) template as the archive's "Capital-Productive Liquid Earnings" and "Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage" and its oiadp/at and oiadp/dp legs are highly correlated.

A direct recombination that takes the archived "Funded Organizational Runway" and replaces its margin leg with the archived oibdp/(dp+xint) coverage leg, offering no new economic mechanism beyond the existing components.
